Its main points are: • [1] The document establishes a bicameral Congress with a Senate (two senators per state, six-year terms) and a House of Representatives (elected every two years). It grants legislative power to this body but no one can be appointed federal office during their term in either house. • [2] Legislation requires passage by both houses and the President's approval; a veto override needs two-thirds of each house, with reconsideration allowed after presidential action. Section 8 authorizes Congress to regulate commerce, coin money, establish post offices, maintain a navy, and exercise exclusive authority over acquired territories. • [3] The Constitution defines the President as head of state for four years, requiring an electoral majority to win or a House vote in case of a tie. The judiciary is vested in a single Supreme Court and inferior courts established by Congress with appellate jurisdiction except for impeachment trials. • [4] Treason is defined as levying war against the US, aiding its enemies, or supplying them; conviction requires two witnesses or open court confession. Punishment must be determined solely by Congress to prevent corruption of blood or forfeiture during an attainted person's lifetime. It also mandates full faith and credit among states, granting citizens freedom to flee another state upon claim, and sets rules for new state admission (consent from both House and legislatures).
